C2 - measured: the minor-tick ladders of the two panels fall on identical pixel rows (227 through 953, one decade = 116.6 px), so the sidecar's shared_scales declaration is true

C6 - two states in Okabe-Ito vermillion and grey, distinguishable in grayscale and redundant with whether the line crosses the drawn 0.05 rule
C7 - the declared unit is the reported test and every line is one test; the counts in the subtitles are at that unit
C9 - every test is drawn individually rather than summarised (see the C4 finding for whether they can be told apart)

findings.observed: The y axis reads 'p-value (log scale); dashed line = 0.05' and the x ticks read 'as published' and 're-analysed'. The sidecar declares that the right position is 'the Benjamini-Hochberg q-value over all 39 tests', so one axis label, one dashed rule and one set of decades are serving a raw p on the left and an adjusted q on the right, and nothing in the image says the quantity changes between the two columns.
findings.fix: Name the quantity at each column - 'p' and 'BH q' on the x tick labels, with the axis label naming both - so the 0.05 rule is read as a significance threshold on the left and an FDR threshold on the right.

findings.observed: Neither panel says how many tests it holds. The only count in the image at that level is '39 tests' in the title; the subtitles give '12 significant as published - 10 after re-analysis' and '21 significant as published - 0 after re-analysis', which are numerators without their denominators. The sidecar's 16 and 23 appear nowhere on the figure.
findings.fix: Print the panel's test count in each subtitle, e.g. '16 tests: 12 significant as published, 10 after re-analysis'.

findings.observed: Part 2 declares 23 tests. Its 're-analysed' column is drawn as three dark shapes, the largest a single fused blob 21 px wide by 102 px tall spanning about q = 0.17 to 0.87 and containing roughly six markers' worth of ink (1695 px against 285 px for one marker). The other columns are no better: 11 and 10 separable blobs where 16 tests are declared, 14 where 23 are. A reader cannot count any column and so cannot check '21 significant' or '0 after re-analysis' against the marks.
findings.fix: Make the markers countable at every column - jitter along x, open markers, or a count printed at each column - so the number of tests in each column can be read off the drawing.

findings.observed: The title asserts 'correcting for 39 tests'. The sidecar states that the paper's blanket statements about unreported comparisons and the side-bias regressions have no reported p-value, 'so 39 is a lower bound on the family'. The figure presents 39 as the denominator of the correction with no sign that the family is incomplete, and a Benjamini-Hochberg q computed over an undercounted family is the anti-conservative direction.
findings.fix: Say on the figure that 39 is the number of reported p-values and a lower bound on the family, and state how many comparisons the paper describes without a p-value.

findings.observed: source_script declares 'workflows/32_fig_wang2026.py'. No such file exists; 32 is 32_recompute_wang2026.py and the figure script is 33_fig_wang2026.py. git_sha is 'f3b98a8-dirty', so the sha does not pin the code either.
findings.fix: Point source_script at the script that wrote the file, and regenerate on a clean tree.

findings.observed: Part 2's whole claim is '0 after re-analysis', and the mark it rests on is drawn centred on the threshold: the lowest 're-analysed' marker's centre is at q = 0.0507 against a dashed rule drawn 3 px thick at 0.0502. At the resolution of the image that mark is on the line, not above it.
findings.fix: Label that one value next to its marker, so the claim does not depend on a distinction the drawing cannot resolve.

findings.observed: Vermillion and grey lines carry the figure's organising distinction and no key, legend or direct label in the image says what either colour means.
findings.fix: Direct-label one vermillion line, e.g. 'crosses 0.05 after re-analysis'.

findings.observed: The note 'values below 1e-06 drawn at 1e-06' does not say how many values were clipped - one marker sits on the floor in Part 1 - and the marker and its grey connecting line are drawn over the note, striking through 'below'.
findings.fix: State the number of clipped values and place the note clear of the floor marker.

findings.observed: The title names Part 2 first and Part 1 second; the panels run Part 1 then Part 2, and the sidecar's n_per_group also lists Part 2 first.
findings.fix: Order the title's clauses, the panels and the sidecar's groups the same way.

sidecar_image_mismatches: axes.y.variable declares 'p-value' while transformations declare the right position is a Benjamini-Hochberg q-value; the image carries only the 'p-value' label, so the sidecar contradicts itself and the image follows the wrong half.
n_per_group declares 16 and 23 tests; the image states neither, and no column resolves into that many separable markers (11/10 in Part 1, 14/3 in Part 2).

missing declares 'none; every reported p-value in the results section is drawn', which holds only with the floor convention the figure annotates; the number of values pushed onto that floor is not declared in either place.
source_script declares workflows/32_fig_wang2026.py, which does not exist in the repository.
shared_scales ('yes; both panels share the log y axis limits and ticks') is confirmed true: identical tick rows 227-953 in both panels.
